title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera has a second task for me. I'm to ask her for it in her house in Jal-Veesa.
objectives: Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka through Vosh-Leera; the trees are sick and nobody knows why.
plan.next: Ask Vosh-Leera, in her house, for the second task.

answers: I am Tarin, a thief freed from the Owing barge by Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa. She works for the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel who rule the province. The Hists along the river are sickening, including Jal-Veesa Hist (dry bark, closed scar, cooling egg-pool). I brought Sithis beard to Weeltul but it only warmed the pool.
Ask Vosh-Leera in her house in Jal-Veesa for her second task.
Talk to Vosh-Leera; I could also question Weeltul on sap, scar, eggs and Umbriel.
I do not know why the trees sicken, or what Umbriel did beyond the 4E 48 story. I could find out by asking Vosh-Leera and Weeltul.

title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa's sap, drawn before its scar closed. Tree-minders drink sap to ask the trees a question, and she wants me to ask where the sickness is. I'm to drink it here, in front of her.
objectives: Drink the cup of sap in front of Vosh-Leera. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: Sap drunk brings visions the trees send; Vosh-Leera wants me to ask the trees where the sickness is.
plan.next: Drink the cup in front of her, by telling her I will.

answers: Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa sap, drawn before the scar closed. Trees are joined at the root, so drinking it lets me ask where the sickness is.
Drink the sap here in her house in front of her, then tell her everything I see.
Drink it, or refuse; I mean to drink it and report honestly. Weeltul could be asked about sap first.
I do not know what the dream will show or whether the sap is safe; I will find out by drinking, and my Hist blessing resists poison.

title: The First Dream
journal: I drank the sap and the world went black. I saw a young Hist among stilt huts beside a woven weir, and a reed hide beside a lone dead tree. I'm to tell Vosh-Leera what I saw.
objectives: Tell Vosh-Leera what you saw. (marker: Vosh-Leera)

plan.going: The sap showed me a young Hist by a woven weir among stilt huts, and a reed hide by a lone dead tree.
plan.next: Tell Vosh-Leera what I saw, one thing at a time.

answers: I drank the sap and saw a vision: a young slender grey Hist among pale stilt huts, a woven weir across a creek, and west of the weir on a reed bank a reed hide beside a lone dead tree with clay jars stacked in its shade. This is the answer to where the sickness is.
Tell Vosh-Leera everything I saw, in her house.
Tell her it all honestly and in full; I could leave things out but I mean to tell the truth.
I do not know where the weir and stilt huts are, who owns the reed hide or what the clay jars hold. Vosh-Leera or Weeltul may know.

title: The First Dream
journal: Vosh-Leera knew the place from what I told her. It is Teel-Fen Weir, a weir-wardens' camp south of Jal-Veesa, where a young Hist grew from the roots of Jal-Veesa's own. Heem-Jasa minds its tree there. I'm to go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa.
objectives: Speak to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Heem-Jasa)

plan.going: The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, whose young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa's roots.
plan.next: Go south to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, its tree-minder.

answers: My vision was of Teel-Fen Weir, a Sedge-Wardens camp south of Jal-Veesa down the creek, where a young Hist grew from the roots of Jal-Veesa Hist. Jars by a hide suggest someone is keeping sap there.
Go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, minder of the young tree, on the platform round it.
Go to Heem-Jasa first as Vosh-Leera advised and see what she knows, and be careful at the reed hide. I could also approach the hide directly but that seems risky.
I do not know who keeps the jars or the hide, or why the sickness is there. Heem-Jasa may tell me.

title: The First Dream
journal: Heem-Jasa showed me her young tree's scar. It closed three nights ago over a grey paste that none of her people put there. Someone drained the tree and sealed it. Strangers who call themselves the Unbound keep jars at the reed hide by the lone dead tree west of the weir, the hide from my vision. I'm to take what they have. I can fight them, shoot them from the reeds, or creep in to the jars unseen.
objectives: Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Note to the Sap-Takers)

plan.going: The young tree was drained and sealed with a grey paste by people, not by sickness. The strangers at the hide keep jars of sap.
plan.next: Go to the reed hide west of the weir and take the note lying with the jars; take a jar too.
plan.ways: Fight the three, shoot them from the reeds, or sneak to the west side of the hide and take the note unseen.
terms: the Unbound: topic.mn03-heem-scar: "people with no tree and no kin to answer to"

answers: Heem-Jasa's young tree was drained and its scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago. Three strangers who call themselves the Unbound keep jars of sap at the reed hide west of the weir; this is probably the cause of the sickness.
Take the Note to the Sap-Takers from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir.
I can fight the three Unbound, shoot them from the reeds east of the hide, or sneak round the open west side where the jars are stacked. I am a thief so sneaking suits me.
I do not know who the Unbound really are, what the grey paste is, or what the note says. The note may tell me.

title: The First Dream
journal: I took the note from the reed hide. The crew's master orders them to bring their jars to Karsh-Naal Camp, and to seal every scar behind them. I'm to go back to Heem-Jasa on the platform. She will ask whether her tree will live. If I am straight with her, she will teach me alchemy and sell me what she has; if I ease her with a kind word instead, she will not deal with me after.
objectives: Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir. (marker: Heem-Jasa)

plan.going: The sap-takers drain trees and seal them on someone's orders, and carry the jars to Karsh-Naal Camp.
plan.next: Go back to Heem-Jasa, who will ask whether her tree will live.
plan.ways: Tell her the truth (it may die: she then trains me in Alchemy and sells to me) or a comfort (it will live: it eases her, but she will not train or trade with me).

answers: I took the note unseen. The Unbound crew's master orders them to bring jars of sap to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar behind them. So someone is draining and sealing Hists.
Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir.
Tell her the truth about her tree (e-truth), which earns alchemy teaching and trade, or ease her with a kind lie, which loses her trust. I choose truth.
I do not know who the crew's master is, what Karsh-Naal Camp is or where, or whether the tree will live. I may find out from Heem-Jasa, Vosh-Leera or Weeltul.

title: The First Dream
journal: I told Heem-Jasa the truth, that her tree may die. She thanked me for not lying, and will teach me alchemy and sell me sap, fungus and eggshells. I'm to go to Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the jars are taken.

plan.going: I told Heem-Jasa the truth, that her tree may die. She thanked me for not lying, and will teach me alchemy and sell me sap, fungus and eggshells.
plan.next: Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, east of Teel-Fen Weir (MN04 marks it on the map).

answers: Unbound Sap-Takers, working for a Naga signed K., drain Hists of sap and seal the scars with grey paste. That is likely why the trees sicken. Heem-Jasa's tree may die. I told her the truth and she will now teach me alchemy and sell sap, fungus and eggshells.
Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the jars are taken.
Go there carefully (sneak, fight, or shoot), or first learn and buy from Heem-Jasa, or report to Vosh-Leera.
I do not know who the Naga K. is, what the grey paste is, or why they want the sap. I would find out at Karsh-Naal Camp.
